methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Kinova Robotics is a late-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Charles Deguire and Louis-Joseph L'Ecuyer that has raised $51.6M to date. The robotics sector contains a meaningful peer set of 9 comparable companies (1 public, 8 private), including firms such as Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics, though few trading comparables exist at Kinova's exact stage and valuation tier.

Valuation triangulation relies primarily on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 1.2x step-up multiplier to the $51.6M total capital raised as a proxy for current value. This method is appropriate for late-stage private companies and yields an implied valuation of $62M. A peer-median approach could not be applied; while 10 robotics peers exist sector-wide, fewer than three qualify as same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with similar valuation tier, making a narrow peer multiple unreliable.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $53M to $71M, centered on $62M. The low end reflects a conservative 1.0x raise multiple; the high end applies a 1.35x uplift. Key uncertainties include the absence of sufficient late-stage robotics comps trading at known multiples and the reliance on a single methodology. Revenue trajectory, cash burn, and product adoption milestones would strengthen conviction but are not available in current data.
